## COMPLETE AbletonOSC NAMESPACE

### 1. APPLICATION (`application.py`)

| OSC Address | Direction | Parameters | Returns | Capability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `/live/application/get/version` | get | (none) | (major_version, minor_version) | Read-only |
| `/live/application/get/average_process_usage` | get | (none) | (cpu_usage) | Read-only |
| `/live/startup` | notification | -- | Sent automatically on init | Outbound only |

---

### 2. SONG (`song.py`)

#### Methods (fire-and-forget, no return value)

All take no parameters unless noted.

| OSC Address | Parameters |
|---|---|
| `/live/song/capture_and_insert_scene` | (none) |
| `/live/song/capture_midi` | (none) |
| `/live/song/continue_playing` | (none) |
| `/live/song/create_audio_track` | (index) |
| `/live/song/create_midi_track` | (index) |
| `/live/song/create_return_track` | (none) |
| `/live/song/create_scene` | (index) |
| `/live/song/delete_return_track` | (index) |
| `/live/song/delete_scene` | (index) |
| `/live/song/delete_track` | (index) |
| `/live/song/duplicate_scene` | (index) |
| `/live/song/duplicate_track` | (index) |
| `/live/song/force_link_beat_time` | (time) |
| `/live/song/jump_by` | (beats) |
| `/live/song/jump_to_prev_cue` | (none) |
| `/live/song/jump_to_next_cue` | (none) |
| `/live/song/redo` | (none) |
| `/live/song/re_enable_automation` | (none) |
| `/live/song/set_or_delete_cue` | (none) |
| `/live/song/start_playing` | (none) |
| `/live/song/stop_all_clips` | (none) |
| `/live/song/stop_playing` | (none) |
| `/live/song/tap_tempo` | (none) |
| `/live/song/trigger_session_record` | (none) |
| `/live/song/undo` | (none) |

#### Read-Write Properties (get/set/start_listen/stop_listen)

For each property `{prop}`, four addresses are registered:
- `/live/song/get/{prop}` -- returns (value)
- `/live/song/set/{prop}` -- params: (value)
- `/live/song/start_listen/{prop}` -- starts listener, sends updates to `/live/song/get/{prop}`
- `/live/song/stop_listen/{prop}` -- stops listener

| Property | Type |
|---|---|
| `arrangement_overdub` | bool |
| `back_to_arranger` | bool |
| `clip_trigger_quantization` | int (enum) |
| `current_song_time` | float (beats) |
| `groove_amount` | float |
| `is_ableton_link_enabled` | bool |
| `loop` | bool |
| `loop_length` | float (beats) |
| `loop_start` | float (beats) |
| `metronome` | bool |
| `midi_recording_quantization` | int (enum) |
| `nudge_down` | bool |
| `nudge_up` | bool |
| `punch_in` | bool |
| `punch_out` | bool |
| `record_mode` | bool |
| `root_note` | int (0-11) |
| `scale_name` | string |
| `session_record` | bool |
| `signature_denominator` | int |
| `signature_numerator` | int |
| `tempo` | float (BPM) |

#### Read-Only Properties (get/start_listen/stop_listen, NO set)

| Property | Type |
|---|---|
| `can_redo` | bool |
| `can_undo` | bool |
| `is_playing` | bool |
| `song_length` | float |
| `session_record_status` | int (enum) |

#### Special Song Endpoints

| OSC Address | Direction | Parameters | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/live/song/get/num_tracks` | get | (none) | (count) |
| `/live/song/get/track_names` | get | (optional: start_index, end_index) | (name1, name2, ...) |
| `/live/song/get/track_data` | get | (track_min, track_max, property_specs...) | Interleaved property values. Property specs: `track.{prop}`, `clip.{prop}`, `clip_slot.{prop}`, `device.{prop}` |
| `/live/song/export/structure` | action | (none) | (1) -- writes JSON to temp dir |
| `/live/song/get/num_scenes` | get | (none) | (count) |
| `/live/song/get/scenes/name` | get | (optional: start_index, end_index) | (name1, name2, ...) |
| `/live/song/get/cue_points` | get | (none) | (name1, time1, name2, time2, ...) |
| `/live/song/cue_point/jump` | action | (index_or_name) | (none) |
| `/live/song/cue_point/add_or_delete` | action | (none) | (none) |
| `/live/song/cue_point/set/name` | set | (cue_index, new_name) | (none) |
| `/live/song/start_listen/beat` | listen | (none) | Sends `/live/song/get/beat` with (beat_number) on each beat |
| `/live/song/stop_listen/beat` | unlisten | (none) | (none) |

### 3. TRACK (`track.py`)

All track endpoints take `(track_index, ...)` as the first parameter. Using `"*"` as track_index queries all tracks.

| `/live/track/delete_device` | (track_index, device_index) |
| `/live/track/stop_all_clips` | (track_index) |

---

# AbletonOSC Ecosystem Research Report

## 1. AbletonOSC Core Project

**Repo:** https://github.com/ideoforms/AbletonOSC
- **Stars:** 707 | **Forks:** 123 | **Open Issues:** 51 | **License:** MIT
- **Language:** Python (MIDI Remote Script)
- **Created:** 2021-05-02 | **Last push:** 2025-11-19
- **Requires:** Ableton Live 11 or above
- **Ports:** Listens on UDP 11000, replies on UDP 11001

**Architecture:** A MIDI Remote Script installed into Ableton's Remote Scripts directory. It exposes the Live Object Model (LOM) via OSC. Tick-based processing (not threaded) -- each Ableton UI tick processes queued OSC messages.

**API Categories:**
- Application (version, logging, test)
- Song (playback, tempo, metronome, cue points, loops, scene/track creation)
- View (selected scene/track/clip/device)
- Track (volume, pan, mute, arm, sends, routing, devices)

# AbletonOSC Complete Technical Reference

## Overview

AbletonOSC is a **MIDI Remote Script** (NOT a Max4Live device) that exposes Ableton Live's Live Object Model (LOM) via Open Sound Control (OSC). It runs as an embedded Python control surface inside Ableton Live.

## Architecture

**Bridge mechanism:** AbletonOSC is a Python `ControlSurface` subclass (`Manager` extends `ableton.v2.control_surface.ControlSurface`). It runs inside Ableton's embedded Python runtime -- no Max4Live required.

**Polling model:** Live's embedded Python does NOT support threading. The `Manager.tick()` method is called every 100ms via `self.schedule_message(1, self.tick)`, which processes all queued UDP datagrams synchronously in a non-blocking loop.

**Handler architecture:**
- `Manager` (manager.py) -- top-level ControlSurface, owns the OSCServer, initializes all handlers
- `OSCServer` (osc_server.py) -- custom UDP socket server (non-blocking), dispatches messages to callbacks by address, sends replies
- `AbletonOSCHandler` (handler.py) -- base Component class with generic `_get_property`, `_set_property`, `_call_method`, `_start_listen`, `_stop_listen`
- Domain handlers: `SongHandler`, `TrackHandler`, `ClipHandler`, `ClipSlotHandler`, `DeviceHandler`, `SceneHandler`, `ViewHandler`, `ApplicationHandler`, `MidiMapHandler`

**Message flow:**
1. Client sends UDP datagram to port 11000
2. `OSCServer.process()` reads from non-blocking socket in a loop
3. Message parsed as `OscMessage` or `OscBundle`
4. Address matched against `_callbacks` dict (exact match or wildcard with `*`)
5. Callback invoked, return value (if any) sent back as response to sender on port 11001
6. Responses sent to `(sender_hostname, 11001)` -- the remote address is updated on each received message

## Installation

- **Requirement:** Ableton Live 11 or above
- **No Max4Live dependency** -- this is a MIDI Remote Script
- Install path:
  - **macOS:** `/Users/[username]/Music/Ableton/User Library/Remote Scripts/AbletonOSC/`
  - **Windows:** `\Users\[username]\Documents\Ableton\User Library\Remote Scripts\AbletonOSC\`
- Select "AbletonOSC" in `Preferences > Link / Tempo / MIDI > Control Surface`

## Port Configuration

| Port | Direction | Binding |
|------|-----------|---------|
| **11000** | Listen (receive from client) | Binds to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) |
| **11001** | Response (send to client) | Sends to `(sender_ip, 11001)` |

Constants defined in `abletonosc/constants.py`:
```python
OSC_LISTEN_PORT = 11000
OSC_RESPONSE_PORT = 11001
```

## Wildcard Support

Any OSC address containing `*` is treated as a wildcard. The `*` matches `[^/]+` (any characters except `/`). This allows queries like `/live/track/get/*` to trigger all matching handlers.

## Listener/Subscription Mechanism

Any property that supports `get` also supports `start_listen` and `stop_listen`:
- **`/live/{domain}/start_listen/{property} [args]`** -- registers a Live API listener via `add_{property}_listener()`. Immediately sends the current value, then sends updates on every change.
- **`/live/{domain}/stop_listen/{property} [args]`** -- removes the listener via `remove_{property}_listener()`.
- **Listener responses** are sent to `/live/{domain}/get/{property}` with the same address prefix as the getter, prepended with the object indices.

## Python Client Library

Bundled `client/client.py` provides `AbletonOSCClient`:
- `send_message(address, params)` -- fire-and-forget
- `query(address, params, timeout=0.150)` -- send and block for response (150ms default timeout, matching one Live tick)
- `send_bundle(messages)` -- send OSC bundle
- `set_handler(address, fn)` -- register callback for incoming messages
- `await_message(address, timeout)` -- block until a specific address is received

Key findings:

**Architecture surprise:** AbletonOSC is a MIDI Remote Script, not a Max4Live device. No M4L dependency — works with Live Standard. Runs inside Ableton's embedded Python with a 100ms tick-based processing loop.

**Namespace:** ~550+ OSC endpoints across 9 domains (Song, Track, Clip, ClipSlot, Device, Scene, View, Application, MidiMap). Full read AND write — you can create clips, add MIDI notes, change device parameters, control transport, modify routing.

**Coverage gap:** Only ~40-50% of the full LOM. Missing: master/return tracks, rack/chain hierarchy, browser integration, automation envelopes, arrangement view details.

**Critical limitations for agent workloads:**
- Single-client only (second client steals responses)
- No request/response correlation IDs
- 100-200ms round-trip latency (tick-bound)
- UDP datagram overflow on large MIDI clips

**Ecosystem reality:** The most popular MCP server (ahujasid, 2.3k stars) **bypasses AbletonOSC entirely** with its own threaded Remote Script using JSON/TCP. Only one significant MCP (Simon-Kansara, 369 stars) actually uses AbletonOSC as transport.

**Strategic recommendation:** Hybrid approach — parse `.als` files (gzipped XML) for deep offline analysis, use OSC (or a custom threaded Remote Script) for live control, and skip the MCP layer entirely for a direct python-osc integration.
